metadata.title: Privacy Policy
metadata.description: How SaaSy Land handles account, payment, newsletter, and technical data, and how to exercise your privacy rights.

title: Privacy Policy
description: How SaaSy Land handles account, payment, newsletter, and technical data, and how to exercise your privacy rights.

controller.title: Who is responsible
controller.body: SaaSy Land at saasyland.com is operated by Piotr Borowiecki, the controller of personal data described here. Contact {email} for privacy questions or requests.

collection.title: What we collect
collection.body:
If you create an account, we store your name, email address, profile image if provided, account settings, and verification status. Passwords are stored as hashes. If you choose Google or GitHub sign-in, we receive the profile and authentication information needed to sign you in. Session records can include your IP address, browser information, and expiry time. Two-factor authentication stores the information needed to secure your account. Rate limiting stores counters keyed by your IP address and the action you attempted, or by a SHA-256 hash of the email address a verification, password-reset, newsletter or withdrawal acknowledgement email was sent to, or of the licence key the CLI presented; each counter expires within an hour.

Purchases create customer, order, and licence records, including the issued key, its status, whether you asked for immediate supply at checkout, and associated activation records. Our database also keeps a copy of each order and subscription that Polar reports for your account, with its product, amount, currency, status, refunds, invoice number, dates and Polar's identifiers. Polar processes licence issuance and activation data; your account displays active machines and lets you release an activation. When you use the saasyland CLI on a machine or in CI, our licence API receives your licence key, a machine identifier and your IP address, which it uses for rate limiting; when you activate, it also receives a label for the machine, its operating system, the CLI version and whether the activation is for a machine or for CI; when the CLI downloads the templates of a release, it also receives that release's version and the answers that describe your project's stack, which it uses only to check the request and does not store. Our database records when your key is first activated and when the CLI first downloads templates with it, as the record that your purchase was delivered. The machine identifier is a keyed SHA-256 hash (HMAC) of your operating system's machine ID, or of your CI provider and repository ID, so the ID itself never leaves your machine. Polar stores the machine identifier and the activation details with the activation; our database does not keep them. If you withdraw from a contract with the withdrawal function, we store the name, email address and order number you give, the language of the page, whether you were signed in, when we received the statement and when we emailed the acknowledgement, the licence and Polar order it matched, and the refund terms that applied to that licence at that moment. Card details are handled by the payment provider. Newsletter records contain your email address, selected language, signup source, subscription status, confirmation and unsubscribe tokens, and related timestamps. If you arrive through an affiliate link, Affonso receives the referral click with your browser's user agent and the referring page, and the referral identifier is added to the Polar order if you buy. Requests also generate security and operational logs.

purposes.title: Why we use it
purposes.body: We use account and purchase information to provide access, authenticate you, deliver what you bought, provide support, and manage licences, including checking a licence and its activated machines when the CLI asks and providing the templates of the release it asks for. We also use purchase information to confirm purchases by email, to receive and acknowledge withdrawals, and to decide refund requests and answer payment disputes with the records of a purchase and its delivery. Transactional emails verify addresses, confirm changes, and help recover accounts. Newsletter emails are sent after you confirm your subscription. Technical information helps prevent abuse, investigate errors, and keep the service reliable.

basis.title: Legal bases
basis.body: Processing needed to provide your account and purchases is based on performance of a contract or steps you request before a contract, under GDPR Article 6(1)(b). Newsletter delivery is based on consent, Article 6(1)(a). Security, abuse prevention, service reliability, keeping delivery records for refunds and payment disputes, and crediting the affiliates who recommend us rely on legitimate interests, Article 6(1)(f). Records required by tax, accounting, or other applicable law, and receiving and acknowledging withdrawal statements under consumer law, are processed to meet legal obligations, Article 6(1)(c). Providing an account email is necessary for account access; joining the newsletter is optional.

providers.title: Service providers and transfers
providers.body:
Cloudflare provides hosting, database, caching, and operational infrastructure. Resend delivers email. Polar handles checkout and payments as merchant of record and processes data under its own privacy notice; we may share a purchase’s delivery records with Polar to answer a refund request or a payment dispute. Affonso records affiliate referrals, only when you arrive through an affiliate link. Google and GitHub are involved only if you choose their sign-in options. We may also disclose information when legally required. We do not sell personal data or share newsletter addresses for another business’s marketing.

These providers may process data outside your country, including outside the EEA. Where required, transfers rely on an applicable adequacy decision or contractual safeguards such as the European Commission’s standard contractual clauses. Contact us for information about the safeguards relevant to your data.

retention.title: How long we keep it
retention.body:
Account data is retained while needed to operate your account and provide support. After an account is deleted, records are removed or anonymised unless retention is required for legal obligations, fraud prevention, or resolving disputes. Payment and accounting records are kept for the legally required period. Delivery records are kept with the licence record for as long as the payment records. Withdrawal statements are kept for as long as the payment records of the purchase they concern; when an account is deleted they are kept no longer linked to it. When an account is deleted, our copies of its orders and subscriptions are kept as payment records, no longer linked to the account but still carrying Polar's customer identifier. Session and security records are retained only while needed for their purpose. Activation details stay with Polar until you release the activation from your account or with the CLI. Rate-limit counters expire within an hour, and expired ones are deleted in batches during later rate-limit checks.

Newsletter information is kept while your subscription is active. An unsubscribed record may be retained to respect your opt-out and prevent accidental resubscription. You can request deletion. Copies in backups or provider systems may remain until their normal retention periods end.

cookies.title: Cookies and local storage
cookies.body:
Essential authentication cookies keep you signed in and support account security. The saasyland.com_locale cookie remembers the language associated with the pages you visit, saasyland.com_theme remembers your theme, sidebar_state remembers for seven days whether the workspace sidebar is open, and regional_pricing remembers whether you turned off a regional price offer. These functions support the service and your choices.

If you open an affiliate link, which carries a parameter such as ?via=, Affonso's script loads for that visit only. It stores the affonso_referral cookie and a visitor identifier in local storage for {cookieDays} days, so the affiliate who recommended us is credited if you buy. The script is not loaded on any other visit.

The application does not add advertising trackers or analytics cookies. External sign-in and payment services have their own storage practices. Blocking essential cookies may prevent sign-in or language preferences from working.

rights.title: Your choices and rights
rights.body:
Depending on the applicable law, you may request access, correction, deletion, restriction, or a portable copy of your data, and object to processing based on legitimate interests. You can withdraw newsletter consent at any time through the unsubscribe link or by contacting us; this does not affect processing that was lawful before withdrawal. We do not make decisions about you solely through automated processing that produces legal or similarly significant effects.

Send requests to {email}. We may need to verify your identity and will respond within the period required by law, normally one month under the GDPR. You may complain to a data protection authority, including Poland’s President of the Personal Data Protection Office (UODO), or the authority where you live or work.

changes.title: Changes to this notice
changes.body: We update this notice when the service or its data practices change. The date above identifies the current version. Where a change requires a separate notice or your consent, we will provide it before applying that change.
